spec.material: a short multiple-choice class test on one lesson objective, taken after the lesson, with its answer key
requirements: Each question has a clear stem that prints every number it asks about, exactly four options keyed A-D and one correct option.
The correct option is the only option that is right by the lesson's own definitions and examples.
No two options of a question say the same thing.
Each wrong option is a mistake a learner could make with the numbers in the stem, written as the answer alone; no filler such as 'Both are equal' or 'Cannot be determined'.
Each of the three wrong options has a short snake_case misconception code naming the specific error a learner who picks it likely holds.
Each question has a difficulty of easy, medium or hard that fits the work it needs.
The two questions test different parts of the objective and stay strictly within it; keep numbers right for the class's grade.
Numbers, units and amounts are plain text; maths symbols go between $ signs only where a symbol is needed.
An objective that names a size, such as billions, is tested at that size in at least one question.
